'''Jesse James Palmer''' (born October 5, 1978)<ref name=NFLprofile>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/jessepalmer/2504732/profile |title=Jesse Palmer| publisher=National Football League | access-date=August 14, 2017}}</ref> is a Canadian television personality, sports commentator, and former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[quarterback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for five seasons. Palmer played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]] under coach [[Steve Spurrier]], and then played professionally for the [[New York Giants]] in the NFL before spending half of the 2006 season with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

Palmer was cast in 2004 as the Bachelor on the [[The Bachelor (American TV series) season 5|fifth season]] of the reality television series ''[[The Bachelor (American TV series)|The Bachelor]]''. He went on to become a college football analyst for [[ESPN]]/[[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] in the United States,<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=http://espnmediazone.com/us/bios/palmer_jesse/| title=Jesse Palmer: College Football Analyst | publisher=[[ESPN]]| access-date= August 14, 2017}}</ref> and has been a contributor to [[The Sports Network]] (TSN) in Canada.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/columnists/jesse_palmer/?id=columnists-jesse_palmer |title=[Columns by Jesse Palmer] | publisher=[[The Sports Network]] |archive-date=July 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130722193747/http://www.tsn.ca/columnists/jesse_palmer/?id=columnists-jesse_palmer}}</ref>  He was also a contributor to ABC's ''[[Good Morning America]]''. In 2018, he hosted the kickoff season of ''[[The Proposal (American TV series)|The Proposal]]'' on [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]]. Since 2017, he has hosted the ''[[Holiday Baking Championship]]'' on [[Food Network]]. He was host of ''DailyMailTV'' from 2017 to 2020. In 2021, Palmer was named as the permanent host of ''The Bachelor'' and ''[[The Bachelorette (American TV series)|The Bachelorette]]''.<ref name=":2" />

'''Jevon Kearse''' (born September 3, 1976), nicknamed "'''the Freak'''", is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] for eleven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the late 1990s and 2000s. Kearse played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and was named the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Defensive Player of the Year in 1998.

Kearse was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the first round pick of the [[1999 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] for four seasons between his two stints with the Titans. During his first five years with the Titans, he was a three-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection and [[NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year]] in 1999. His speed (4.43-second [[40-yard dash]]) and {{convert|86|in|cm|adj=on}} wingspan, coupled with a {{convert|37|in|cm|adj=on}} [[vertical leap]], greatly impressed coaches and earned him the nickname "the Freak".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=ST&s_site=dfw&p_multi=ST&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EAF92482B018CAB&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|title=Star Telegram: Search Results|website=nl.newsbank.com}}</ref>

'''Manase Jesse Sapolu''' (born March 10, 1961) is a Samoan former professional [[American football]] player in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played both center and offensive guard, and played his entire career for the [[San Francisco 49ers]].

Sapolu attended [[Farrington High School]] and the [[University of Hawaii]] in [[Honolulu]].  Standing 6 feet 4 inches, 278 lbs., he was selected by the [[Oakland Invaders]] in the 17th round (199th pick overall) of the [[1983 USFL draft]], and selected by 49ers in the 11th round (289th pick overall) of the [[1983 NFL draft]].  He signed with the 49ers on July 10, 1983.

Sapolu is one of six 49ers to own four [[Super Bowl]] championship rings ([[Super Bowl XIX|1984]], [[Super Bowl XXIII|1988]], [[Super Bowl XXIV|1989]], and [[Super Bowl XXIX|1994]]), and the only one of those to earn a ring with the [[1994 San Francisco 49ers season|'94 team]] rather than their first title in [[Super Bowl XVI|1981]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Janower |first=Jacob |date=8 February 2021 |title=Super Bowl winners by player: Who has the most rings in NFL history? |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/super-bowl-wins-by-player-most-rings-nfl-history/1iouj3efoz32o1moq05touj0vz |access-date=29 December 2021 |website=Sporting News}}</ref>  He earned [[Pro Bowl]] honors in 1993 and 1994.

Since retiring in 1997, Sapolu and his wife Lisa have lived in [[Southern California]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://articles.dailypilot.com/2013-02-01/sports/tn-dpt-0201-jesse-sapolu-super-bowl-20130131_1_jesse-sapolu-heart-defect-motivational-speaker |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714153653/http://articles.dailypilot.com/2013-02-01/sports/tn-dpt-0201-jesse-sapolu-super-bowl-20130131_1_jesse-sapolu-heart-defect-motivational-speaker |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |title=Sapolu remains passionate, humble |first=Steve |last=Virgen |newspaper=Daily Pilot |location=Orange County, California |date=February 1, 2013 }}</ref> and remains active in the community as well with the 49ers alumni.

Sapolu has been an integral part in establishing the Polynesian Pro Football Hall of Fame, of which he is a co-founder. He now runs Men In The Trenches (MITT) in California.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MITT 2020 Opening Day - February 2020 |url=http://sapolumeninthetrenches.com/index.html}}</ref>

He played professionally for the [[Houston Oilers]] of the AFL and was named an [[American Football League All-Star game|AFL All-Star]] in 1969.{{Citation needed|date=June 2021}} He later played in the NFL for the Oilers and [[San Diego Chargers]].

Beirne lived in [[Fredericksburg, Texas]].

Jim has two sons, [[Kevin Beirne]], a Major League Baseball right-handed pitcher from 2000 to 2006, and Mike Beirne, a wide receiver and linebacker at the University of Kentucky from 1998 to 2001.{{Citation needed|date=June 2021}}
